name: Reconstruction Era Historical Park (National Monument)
author: parks-page-legacy
summary: Reconstruction Era National Historical Park in Beaufort County, South Carolina, was established in 2017 as the first unit of the National Park System dedicated to the Reconstruction era (1861–1900). The park preserves sites in and around Beaufort associated with the transition from slavery to freedom, including the Brick Baptist Church — where formerly enslaved people first learned to read — and the Darrah Hall at Penn Center, one of the first schools for freed African Americans in the South. The Sea Islands of South Carolina were among the earliest places where the federal government experimented with programs for formerly enslaved people, including land redistribution, education, and political participation. The park tells the stories of newly freed people who built schools, churches, and communities and exercised their rights as citizens during this transformative period.
